{{short description|Biologist, biotechnologist and lecturer}}
'''Gabriele Berg''' (born 1963) is a biologist, biotechnologist and university lecturer in Environmental and Ecological Technology at the [[Graz University of Technology|Technical University of Graz]]. Her research emphasis is on the development of sustainable methods of plant vitalisation with [[Bioeffector]]s and molecular analysis of microbial processes in the soil, particularly in the [[Rhizosphere]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://online.tugraz.at/tug_online/visitenkarte.show_vcard?pPersonenGruppe=3&pPersonenId=1AC5BD1F755830CD|title=Visitenkarte von Berg, Gabriele; Univ.-Prof. Dipl.-Biol. Dr.rer.nat. – TUGRAZonline – Technische Universität Graz|website=online.tugraz.at|accessdate=27 December 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.academia-net.org/profil/prof-dr-gabriele-berg/1133592|title=Prof. Dr. Gabriele Berg – AcademiaNet|website=www.academia-net.org|accessdate=27 December 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.acib.at/de/contacts/gabriele-berg/ |title=Gabriele Berg on Austrian Center of Industrial Biotechnologie |access-date=11 December 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161203194933/http://www.acib.at/de/contacts/gabriele-berg/ |archive-date=3 December 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Life and work ==
She was born in [[Potsdam]], [[East Germany]] in 1963. After graduating from the Helmholtz-Gymnasium, Potsdam  in 1981 Frau Berg studied biology at the [[University of Rostock]]. She graduated with honours (1986) and then spent a research study year in Microbiology and Biotechnology at the [[University of Greifswald]]. In 1995 she obtained the qualification Dr. rer nat with "magna cum laude" and in 2001 the Venia Legendi for [[Microbiology]] with her dissertation Antagonistic Micro-organisms. In 2003 she was awarded a Heisenberg-Stipendium by the [[Deutschen Forschungsgemeinschaft]] (German Research Community). In 2005 she became the first female professor of natural science at the [[Graz University of Technology]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.derstandard.at/consent/tcf/2165336/tu-graz-erste-professorin-in-den-naturwissenschaften|title=derStandard.at|website=www.derstandard.at|accessdate=27 December 2021}}</ref>

== Memberships and affiliations ==
*Senate of the TU Graz
*International Verticillium Steering Committee
*Austrian Society for Biomedical Engineering (ÖGBMT), Vorsitz der Sektion Süd
*[[Deutsche Phytomedizinische Gesellschaft]] (DPG – German Phytomedical Society), chairperson of the working group Biologische Bekämpfung (Biological Control, 2004–2012)
*Editorial Board FEMS Microbial Ecology (2000–2010), MPMI, ISME Journal (2007–)

== Field of interest ==
Frau Berg's research is focused on the environmental biotechnology, in particular the development of sustainable biotechnological methods to improve the microbiological performance potential of soil that has been intensively used for agriculture, and for biological plant protection with plant fortifiers and Biostimulants.

== Awards ==
* Science2Business Award Austria
* ÖGUT Umweltpreis
* Fast Forward Award Styria

== Publications ==
